results.content:
I have considered changing the system over to actually track which is the last page you've seen, although one thing is that if you just go to the homepage of a webcomic you're subscribed to, and that's set to "latest page", it would not remember your place at all then anymore, since it would get overwritten with the latest page. Not sure how much of a problem this would be in practice. I guess it could also not update the last read page if there's any inbetween that you did not read. I dunno, but right now it just goes by when you clicked. So it's not really a bug, it's intended behavior, although the intended behavior is perhaps not entirely ideal. I do want to update that to make the tracking a bit more reliable independent of whether you clicked your sub notif or a link from someplace [...] whether you clicked your sub notif or a link from someplace else. I would appreciate input on how people think it should work, especially in regards to that thing about the latest page frontpage, since right now it will reliably remmber the last page you read, as long as you always use the link from the subs page/tab. results.title: Email Notifications Not Working? Fix Guide 2026 | Mailbird
results.content:
What makes this particularly frustrating is the lack of transparency. Most users discovered their notifications stopped working only after missing important deadlines, overlooking urgent client communications, or failing to respond to time-sensitive requests. The systems provided no error messages, no warnings, and no indication that anything was wrong—notifications simply stopped arriving.

### The Silent Infrastructure Changes That Broke Your Notifications [...] Android 16 users face a particularly frustrating notification crisis caused by critical bugs in the notification system itself. According to detailed analysis of Android 16 notification failures, the core issue manifests as a bug that completely mutes notification sounds when any existing notification remains in the notification shade.

### The Critical Audio Muting Bug

This means that after receiving a first notification of the day, every subsequent email alert arrives silently, forcing users to constantly check their phone rather than being automatically notified of important communications. For professionals who depend on timely email responses, this bug transforms smartphones from productivity tools into sources of constant anxiety and missed opportunities. [...] If you've been missing critical emails, wondering why your phone isn't alerting you to important messages, or feeling frustrated by silent notifications that used to work perfectly, you're not alone. Throughout 2025 and into 2026, millions of professionals have experienced unprecedented disruptions to email notification systems across iOS, Android, Windows, and major email platforms. These aren't minor glitches—they're fundamental infrastructure changes that have left users unable to receive time-sensitive communications, security alerts, and urgent business emails.

results.title: Complaints and Notifications Policy - Policies - Department of Education
results.content:
People making complaints and notifications are provided an outcome advising of the Department’s resolution of the matter.

Complaints and notifications can be made anonymously.

If a complaint or notification remains anonymous, every effort will be made to provide an outcome. This communication can be made by the Department either verbally or in writing.

People making complaints or notifications can elect to report the matter to another relevant agency at any time. Suggested relevant agencies include: [...] The Department encourages any person, other than a staff member as described in section 235(1) of the School Education Act 1999 (WA), to make a complaint to facilitate improved learning, best practice and high-quality service delivery.

The Department strives to resolve complaints and notifications efficiently, equitably and locally where possible.

Complaints and notifications may require referral or reporting to another Division within the Department or to another agency external to the Department for action and legislative compliance. In some instances, the external agency may be responsible for the complaint or notification resolution.

Complaints and notifications can be made verbally or in writing to the Department. [...] categorise complaints and notifications according to the Complaints and Notifications Framework
 encourage staff members to make notifications relating to the conduct of staff members, contractors and volunteers to enable appropriate action in response to fraud and corruption risks and in relation to concerns for the safety of students, parents, carers, staff members, contractors, volunteers and others
 manage complaints and notifications in a fair, equitable, transparent, accessible, culturally responsive, restorative and effective way
 apply procedural fairness in the management of complaints and notifications
 support students in making a complaint and manage complaints involving students with student safety and wellbeing in mind
